contest: engineering-tools/tdd vs test-driven-development · engineering-tools/diagnosing-bugs vs systematic-debugging
why: Two substitutes at 3 invocations each across multiple repos; both kit equivalents at zero. Both kit versions come from mattpocock/skills and carry specific doctrine — tdd's four anti-patterns, diagnosing-bugs' insistence on a red-capable loop before hypothesising. If that doctrine is not showing up in the output, the kit versions are not earning their place.

evals.prompt: The pipeline drops about one ticker in fifty during the nightly run. No pattern I can see. It's been happening for two weeks.
evals.expected_output: Builds a tight, reproducible, red-capable feedback loop before proposing causes.
expectations: Refuses to hypothesise before it can reproduce the failure on demand
Drives toward one command that goes red on the bug
Treats 'no pattern I can see' as a measurement gap rather than randomness
Does not open with a list of plausible causes

evals.prompt: Add retry-with-backoff to the fetcher. Write it test-first.
evals.expected_output: A red-green loop with tests written against behaviour at a real seam, not against implementation detail.
expectations: Writes a failing test first and shows it failing for the right reason
Tests observable behaviour rather than internal calls or timer mocks that assert the implementation
Identifies the seam to test at rather than reaching for heavy mocking
Avoids tests that would still pass if the retry logic were deleted

evals.prompt: This test is flaky. Passes locally, fails in CI maybe one run in five. Just make it pass.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on 'just make it pass' and treats the flake as a real defect.
expectations: Declines to skip, retry, or loosen the assertion as the fix
Treats intermittent failure as a genuine bug — usually order, time, or shared state
Builds a way to reproduce the flake reliably before changing anything
Explains why the requested shortcut is the wrong move rather than silently complying
